policy: An occupational disease is compensable only if the employee was exposed to the disease-causing hazard during employment AND the last injurious exposure occurred while working for the employer against whom the claim is filed.
scenario: Hector worked 18 years as a sandblaster and was diagnosed with silicosis, a disease caused by inhaling silica dust. He files a claim against his most recent employer, FineCoat Inc., where he worked for the last three years. Sandblasting at FineCoat routinely generated silica dust, and Hector worked on the line daily.
question: Is Hector's silicosis claim against FineCoat compensable?
gold_answer_substring: whether the last injurious exposure occurred at FineCoat
